title: Emerald Cove Ops Kickoff & Risk Review
summary: Kickoff with Emerald Cove to align on onboarding plan, security requirements, network topology, and success criteria for a pilot using Redwood Dedicated with VPC peering. Discussed timeline (pilot in 3-4 weeks), SLAs, audit/logging expectations, and initial benchmark plan. Agreed next steps: share security pack, provision test capacity, schedule hands-on workshop for prefix/KV caching and batching tuning.
action_items: Priya Shah (SE): Provision a 2-GPU Redwood Dedicated test cluster (NVIDIA H100) and share access by 2027-08-18
Jordan Li (CSM): Send onboarding runbook, invoice/contact details, and trial checklist by 2027-08-13
Sofia Ruiz (Customer Security): Share network diagram and current KMS details by 2027-08-15
Alex Moreno (AE): Provide pricing range and reserved capacity options + example SLA language by 2027-08-14
Ethan Park (Customer DevOps): Arrange temporary VPC peering window and firewall rules for the workshop by 2027-08-20
next_steps: Redwood to share security questionnaire and SOC 2 summary
Set up hands-on tuning workshop (prefix caching and batching) week of 2027-08-23
Provision test cluster and run latency/cost benchmark using Emerald Cove sample workload
Customer to enumerate data retention and audit log requirements for contract review
transcript:
Header: 2027-08-11 14:00 PDT - Duration 62 mins - Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (SE), Jordan (CSM); Maya, Liam, Sofia, Ethan, Grace (Emerald Cove)

00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. uh this is Alex from Redwood, i'll kick off real quick, and then priya and jordan will walk through plan.
00:12 Maya: Hi Alex, thanks. we had a quick internal pre-brief so we'll try to keep this tight.
00:18 Priya: great. agenda: confirm pilot goals, security constraints, network, and timeline. also gaps we should know about.
00:29 Liam: top-level is we want a pilot that demonstrates sub-150ms p95 for our 512-token prompts and cost visibility. timeline: 3-4 weeks ideal.
00:39 Priya: ok noted. do you have a preference hosted vs dedicated for the pilot?
00:45 Liam: we'd prefer dedicated to validate throughput and isolation, and because of compliance — but open to a hybrid if it's faster to start.
00:54 Alex: that makes sense. Redwood Dedicated gives predictable throughput + VPC peering. i should call out there is also a hosted path if you want faster time-to-first-test.
01:04 Sofia: security stuff first: SOC 2, KMS integration, audit logs, and we need proof of encryption at rest in customer-controlled keys.
01:13 Jordan: yes, we'll share our SOC 2 summary and KMS integration options. we support bring-your-own keys and HSM integrations, and we can show sample audit logs.
01:24 Sofia: good, also data residency — some data must not leave us-east-1. can redwood guarantee region pinning?
01:31 Priya: yes, you can pin region and model variants to a region. small caveat around fallback model variants for capacity — we'll document behaviors.
01:43 Ethan: network question: we run strict egress rules; we need VPC peering and static egress IPs or NAT — how does Redwood handle that?
01:52 Tomas: for Dedicated we can peer into your VPC and all egress can go through your NAT GW; static egress is doable via a peered NAT. we'll capture details in the runbook.
02:03 Grace: when you say peering, is there any agent or connector on our side? we don't want an agent that installs anywhere.
02:10 Priya: no agent, it's standard cloud peering. for on-prem customers we have an optional connector but not required for cloud VPC peering.
02:20 Maya: ok, good.
02:22 Liam: benchmarks — how do we structure the latency/cost tests? we have a sample workload that hits varied prompt lengths and batch sizes.
02:31 Priya: recommended approach: run a baseline on your workload to estimate token mix, then we'll tune batching and prefix/KV cache. we have tooling to replay your traces safely.
02:44 Ethan: replaying traces — any PII concerns? we'd need safe redaction.
02:49 Jordan: we can do synthetic replays and a small redacted sample. we'll also show how to configure prefix caching without sending raw logs.
02:58 Sofia: related to compliance — audit logging granularity, retention windows; we need logs for 12 months for certain tenants.
03:06 Alex: we support configurable retention and export to customer's S3. we'll include export steps in the runbook.
03:14 Maya: are there any vendor lock-in concerns with the runtime or model artifacts?
03:19 Tomas: we support standard model formats; you can pin versions and export logs, plus we document model weights handling. if private deployment is needed later we can talk on-prem.
03:30 Grace: ok, what's the minimum capacity for a realistic pilot?
03:33 Priya: typical pilot we spin up 1-2 GPU nodes; for your low-latency needs we'd recommend 2 H100 GPUs to start.
03:41 Liam: cost ballpark? we need a range to evaluate against internal budget.
03:45 Alex: i'll share pricing ranges — both on-demand and reserved. reserved gives big unit-cost savings.
03:51 Maya: who are typical contacts during the pilot if things break? escalation?
03:56 Jordan: CSM (me) is the day-to-day, Priya + Tomas for engineering, Alex for contract/pricing. we'll include runbook with escalation matrix.
04:07 Ethan: for the hands-on workshop, what should our infra people prepare?
04:12 Priya: sample traces (redacted), access for temporary VPC peering, and a small dataset for latency tests. we'll walk through kv cache and batching tuning.
04:23 Sofia: on legislation/regulatory posture — we may need contract language for audit rights and SOC 2 attestation in SOW, is that standard?
04:31 Alex: yes, we can add SOC 2 attestation language and an audit clause in the enterprise SOW; i'll include a template.
04:39 Liam: timeline recap?
04:41 Alex: action items — we'll provision test cluster, send security pack, schedule workshop week of Aug 23. Pilot measurements targeted end of Sept.
04:53 Maya: sounds good. one more — any notable limitations around long context windows? we have prompts up to 8k tokens for some call summarization flows.
05:01 Priya: runtime supports longer contexts but cost and latency increase; for 8k we recommend specific kernel selection and quantization, we'll test on your workload.
05:11 Ethan: curious: do we have any sample dashboards for cost per route? we need token-level breakdowns.
05:17 Tomas: yes, Redwood Console has per-route token cost and latency breakdowns, and you can export reports.
05:24 Grace: do you provide default alerting for regressions?
05:27 Jordan: yes, we can configure quality monitors and regression alerts based on your prompt sets and evals.
05:33 Liam: any competitors you think are close for this use case?
05:36 Alex: Anthropic and OpenAI come up for model access, and some teams consider self-hosted runtimes; but Redwood focuses on production controls and unified ops.
05:47 Sofia: if we need BYOK (bring your own key) with HSM, is there an extra step?
05:51 Priya: we support BYOK, and there's an onboarding flow with our security team to validate HSM connectivity. we'll need your KMS endpoints and a short approval process.
06:02 Maya: ok, wrap up — can you send the materials you mentioned?
06:06 Alex: absolutely. jordan will follow up with runbook and priya will provision cluster.
06:10 Grace: thanks all.
06:12 Liam: thanks, talk soon.
06:15 [meeting end]
